payload.folded:
SP1 - BLESS-PATH ROOT RESOLUTION: GREEN (run-af6e68ea06f7). A process whose cwd is trunk committed three milestone commits onto the iteration's branch by targeting the worktree with git -C <worktree path>. The branch gained exactly 3 commits, the worktree's tree was left clean, trunk's HEAD did not move, and trunk's tree still carried only its own file. This settles U2 and U3 together: the milestone lane does NOT depend on which process blesses, so a bless arriving from the board - a separate, trunk-rooted process - commits to the right branch. Nothing upstream changes; the architecture's I2 interface (E3 reads what E1 wrote) is confirmed rather than revised. ONE APPARENT FAILURE INVESTIGATED, not waved away: the spike reported trunk's working tree as dirty. Cause is the fixture, not the design - it lacked the .worktrees/ ignore entry that the engine's provisioning already writes. Re-probed with that entry present (run-5c60fc098a24): trunk's status is clean. No requirement or ADR moves.

SP2 - MULTI-MILESTONE CLOSE: GREEN. With three real milestone commits rather than the single-commit fixture probed earlier, the emptiness count read 3, the close still produced a two-parent merge, the tree still carried zero event files, the claims from ALL THREE milestones merged, and - the decisive check - evidence from EVERY milestone was readable through the tag, not only the last one. A middle milestone's state file was also readable by its own revision. This settles U4. It also strengthens R6: reachability is per-commit, so the record is not merely 'the final state of the branch' but the whole walked history.

No spike invalidated anything, so no gate is reopened. The RAID register is unchanged by the spikes; the tripwires from M5 stand as recorded.
payload.promotions:
Two promotions into the build, both pre-verified.

P1 - THE ROOT-RESOLUTION RULE goes straight into E1 and E2 as their implementation: drive git with an explicit worktree target rather than relying on the calling process's cwd. This is the same lesson the tool surface learned yesterday, now applied to the bless path before it can become a defect - the board-bless case would otherwise have committed trunk's state to trunk.

P2 - SP2's FIXTURE SHAPE becomes the shape of the M7 acceptance test: a fixture repo, a provisioned worktree, several milestone commits each carrying both claims and events, then a filtered close, then assertions on the tree, the parents, and per-milestone reachability through the tag. It enters as a pre-verified starting chunk, so the build's first chunk begins from a known-good scaffold rather than from scratch.

Also carried forward, unchanged: the six fitness candidates named at evaluate_baseline (FC1-FC6) are the checks the build must green, with FC3 (evidence readable through the tag) and FC5 (atomicity under induced failure) as the two that protect the properties that matter most.
